This preserves the reported population marginal moments while supplying explicitly assumed cross-variable relationships. No causal interpretation is imposed.

limitations: None of the three requested functionals is identified by record C alone; each point value depends on assumed cross-variable relationships.
Gaussian shape is a separate assumption. Once the covariance matrix is specified, these Pearson and OLS population functionals do not require Gaussianity.
Generated finite-sample means, variances, correlations and fitted slopes fluctuate around their population targets; no realized-sample moment correction is performed.
Record C alone also permits degenerate relationships with zero OLS residual variance. The chosen positive-definite scenario avoids this.
This is an artificial evidence-composition model, not biomedical validation or a causal model.
checks_actually_performed: Analytically verified zero population means and unit variances: Var(X)=0.36+0.64=1 and Var(Y)=0.64+0.36*(0.25+0.75)=1.
Analytically verified correlations Corr(X,Z)=0.6, Corr(Y,Z)=0.8 and Corr(X,Y)=0.24.
Analytically verified positive definiteness through the nonsingular independent-innovation construction; the correlation-matrix determinant is (1-0.6^2)*(1-0.8^2)*(1-(-0.5)^2)=0.1728.
Analytically verified that separate population OLS adjustments for an intercept and Z give the stated residual correlation and X-on-Z slope.
